title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: what an amended declaration may change and how often
content:
## Rule
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product a declaration is amended only by a new declaration the shipper signs, which only the shipper can do. An amendment may change only the particulars on the category's list of amendable particulars; a change of IMDG class, or of any particular outside that list, needs the application to be withdrawn and a new one submitted. After approval an amendment is possible only when the category allows amendments after approval, and it returns the acceptance to review. An acceptance takes at most the category's maximum number of signed amendments. The declared gross weight may change by no more than the category's maximum percentage of the weight before the amendment, and the container count may rise only when the category allows a rise, always within the per-shipper sailing allotment.

## Counting signed amendments
The count covers the amendment declarations on the acceptance's declaration file whose outcome is signed, over the life of the acceptance, before the amendment being handled. It is read from the line's records of that acceptance.

## Decision table
| Request | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Change of a particular on the category's list | may proceed, subject to the other limits |
| Change of IMDG class | the application is withdrawn and a new one submitted |
| Change of a particular not on the list | the application is withdrawn and a new one submitted |
| Amendment after approval, category allows it | possible; the acceptance returns to review |
| Amendment after approval, category does not allow it | not possible |
| Container count rise, category does not allow a rise | not possible |

## Worked cases (hypothetical limits: 8 percent weight change, 4 signed amendments)
- Weight before the amendment 20000 kg: 8 percent of it is 1600 kg, so an amended weight from 18400 kg to 21600 kg stays within the limit; 21700 kg does not.
- Signed amendments already counted: 3. The amendment being handled would be the fourth, which is within 4. Already counted: 4 — a fifth would exceed the maximum and is not taken.

## Points of judgement
- *Is the weight limit measured against the weight first declared?* No; against the weight before the amendment being handled.
- *Does a declaration awaiting signature count towards the maximum?* No; only amendment declarations whose outcome is signed are counted.
